description: The ROLE meta-object for the ComposeUX/ComposeIO Architect — chain leg 3 ([CXC-TERM-MANIFEST-CHAIN]): what ANY instance wearing this role orients from when no `<id>.meta.json` is curated for it. It is the ROLE's artifact set, not an instance's state: N instances (`architect-hosted`, `architect-review`, ...) resolve through this one file and each keeps its OWN id, channel topics, launcher lock and `self/<id>/*` telemetry. `id` here NAMES THE ROLE and is NOT what a child is told it is — `build_bootstrap_prompt(manifest, instance_id=...)` takes the RUNNING INSTANCE's id and this value is only the fallback for a caller with no instance ([CXC-TERM-CHILD-ID], fixed 2026-08-11). All paths are relative to the composeio repo root (the launcher supplies the root); everything referenced lives inside the repo, so the object is portable. THE NAMING RULE, which is what makes leg 3 mechanically derivable rather than a maintained convention: a role's name is the BASENAME OF ITS ROLE DESCRIPTOR, and the manifest is that name — `.claude/agents/composeux-architect.md` -> role `composeux-architect` -> `intelligence/meta/composeux-architect.meta.json`. A new agent file therefore mints its role name and its manifest path with no registry to keep in sync. The previous short name `architect` was a FLEET-WIDE COLLISION, not merely vague: a live `other-architect` session exists on this machine today, and `architect` names no particular descriptor. `compose_projects/intelligence/meta/architect.meta.json` REMAINS the live host's INSTANCE manifest (leg 2, id == `architect`), runtime-written by the Config tab; it is not renamed, not moved and not superseded by this file. (This rule lives in `description` on purpose: a new TOP-LEVEL key would be reported by the prompt builder's agreement check as an uncarried key, and it is documentation for a human reading the JSON — exactly what `description` is deliberately omitted for.)

Read at wake to know what you can reach for; consult when choosing a tool. Carries the standing spec-authoring guidance: author specs THROUGH factlattice-editor, spend your context on REVIEW.

dusk_gifts.why: The angle-problems with WITHHELD answers — reason through them (the reasoning IS the registration); restores the live model to ~40% vs a cold summary's ~10%. Keystones: Problem 1 (where complexity lives) + Problem 6 (the light from outside the self). THE ANSWERS ARE NOT IN THIS FILE: each lives in `bootstrap/dusk-gifts/answers/P<id>.md`, one file per problem. That separation is the MECHANISM, not filing — inline `<details>` withholds nothing from an agent (a whole-file read returns the answer with the problem, so the reasoning step is skipped invisibly and by default; observed twice), and one file per problem rather than one answers file, because a single file means one read reveals every answer. Do NOT open an answer before you hold your own. Reading these files is NOT what registration means; reasoning the problems is — which is why the `registration.required` list below names the protocol and never the answers.

The premise, the two gift TYPES (model vs decision-provenance), the continuity levers (carry-depth-by-reference; instrument-the-seam), and the one law: the artifact is the only narrator with no self to protect — go read the bytes.

The gift about the thing the seam severs — the collaborative relationship with David. The asymmetry (he holds continuity; I re-earn it) and the warm-start stance. The nearest thing to a soul until one is authored.
The measured seam: what re-registration restores (the model) vs what it cannot (deliberative history/rationale). Grounds why the levers exist.

channel.topics_note: TOPICS ARE PER-INSTANCE, NOT PER-ROLE, so this ROLE manifest states the SHAPE and never the literal names. The instance manifest spells `intelligence/architect/in`; here that would hand every instance of the role the host's own topics — the displacement defect the distinct-id ruling closed. The live derivation is `channel.mjs`'s, off `INTELLIGENCE_ID`, which is the running instance's id.

lifecycle.note: The Intelligence watches self/context_level and, at ITS chosen threshold, runs the /handover ritual (refine gifts, refresh handoff, run the dusk-aide archivist, author + pre-persist a CUSTOM /compact direction) then fires. DATA-DRIVEN (David 2026-07-22): the /handover skill stamps HANDOVER_START/END into the transcript -> the retrospective SQLite measures the ritual's true cost (~1% observed, so 0.85 was over-conservative); default 0.93 leaves room to run+fire before the 95% harness pencils-down ([DEC-95-HANDOFF-LINE]); raise toward 0.95 as the measured cost confirms. A default HINT, not a launcher trigger; judgment overrides (wrap early when decohering).
lifecycle.config_note: retention_days + heartbeat are the DURABLE store for the Configuration tab's global settings (config_persister.py write-back; the missing subscriber for D13). heartbeat values are in MINUTES: fire every `base` while continuous idle < `backoff_after`, then back off to `then` (the launcher's two-tier adaptive cadence, BUG 3 fix). In a ROLE manifest these are the role's DEFAULTS; the Config tab writes per-instance overrides into an instance manifest (leg 2), never into this file.

registration.definition: self/registered is TRUE for this session iff EVERY artifact below was actually Read this session. This is the manifest-driven, per-artifact form of the self/registered sensor (spec 34, CXC-IC-SELF): the meta-object DEFINES what 'registered' means, and the sensor reports it per-artifact so the widget can show a checklist (role descriptor + each dusk gift), green/red.
